Then Allah the Exalted revealed: ﴿By the night when it covers﴾ up to His saying: ﴿Indeed, your efforts are diverse﴾ [See: Ibn Kathir 4/520–521; al-Wahidi, Asbab al-Nuzul, p. 523; al-Durr al-Manthur 8/532–533], [meaning the effort of] Abu al-Dahdah and the Ansari, owner of the palm tree.

﴿As for him who gives and fears [Allah]﴾ [meaning Abu] al-Dahdah, ﴿and believes in the best [reward]﴾ [the reward], ﴿We will ease him toward ease﴾, meaning Paradise. ﴿But as for him who is stingy and considers himself self-sufficient﴾, meaning the Ansari, ﴿and denies the best [reward]﴾, meaning the reward, ﴿We will ease him toward hardship﴾, meaning the Fire.

Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 92, verse 11–17:

﴿And his wealth will not avail him when he falls [into the Fire]﴾ — the wealth he withheld. "When he falls" (tarradda): Mujahid said: when he dies. Qatadah and Abu Salih said: he plunges into Jahannam.

﴿Indeed, upon Us is guidance﴾ — meaning clarification (al-bayan). Al-Zajjaj said: it is upon Us to make clear the path of guidance from the path of misguidance. This is also the view of Qatadah, who said: upon Allah is the clarification of what is lawful and what is unlawful.

Al-Farra' said: it means that whoever follows guidance, then upon Allah is its path (sabil), like His saying, ﴿And upon Allah is the direction of the path﴾ [al-Nahl: 9]. He says: whoever seeks Allah, then he is upon the straight path.[[See: Ma'ani al-Qur'an by al-Farra': 3/271.]]

It has also been said that its meaning is: indeed, upon Us is [the guidance and the misguidance], like His saying, ﴿In Your hand is the good﴾ [Al 'Imran: 26]. [He restricted mention to guidance because the context indicates it, like His saying, ﴿Garments that protect you from the heat﴾ [al-Nahl: 81], where He mentioned only the heat and did not mention the cold, because the former indicates the latter.]

﴿And indeed, to Us belong the Hereafter and the former [life]﴾ — whoever seeks them from other than their Owner has indeed erred from the path.

﴿So I have warned you﴾ — O people of Makkah — ﴿of a Fire that blazes fiercely, which none will enter except the most wretched﴾ — meaning: it flares (tatalaza), i.e., it blazes and flames intensely.

﴿The one who denied﴾ the Messenger, ﴿and turned away﴾ from faith.

﴿But the most righteous will be kept away from it﴾ — by "the most wretched" (al-ashqa) he means the wretched one (al-shaqiy), and by "the most righteous" (al-atqa) he means the righteous one (al-taqiy).

**Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 92, verse 18:**

﴿The one who gives his wealth﴾: he gives his wealth. ﴿Seeking purification﴾: he seeks to be pure (zakiyyan) in the sight of Allah, not for show and not for reputation. This refers to Abu Bakr al-Siddiq, according to the consensus.

Ibn al-Zubayr said: Abu Bakr used to buy the weak (among the slaves) and free them. His father said: "My son, if only you would buy those who could protect your back!" He said: "I want only the protection of my own back." So there was revealed: ﴿And the most righteous will be kept away from it﴾, to the end of the surah. [[Narrated by al-Tabari: 30/221. Sahib al-Durr al-Manthur (8/535) added its attribution to Ibn Asakir. Al-Wahidi also mentioned it in Asbab al-Nuzul, p. 526.]]

Muhammad ibn Ishaq mentioned: Bilal belonged to some of the Banu Jumah. He was Bilal ibn Rabah, and his mother's name was Hamama. He was sincere in Islam and pure of heart. Umayya ibn Khalaf used to take him out when the midday heat intensified, lay him on his back in the valley of Makkah, then order a huge rock to be placed upon his chest. Then he would say to him: "You will remain like this until you die, or you disbelieve in Muhammad." In that trial he would say: "One! One!" (Ahad, ahad.)

Muhammad ibn Ishaq also said, from Hisham ibn Urwa, from his father, who said: Abu Bakr passed by him one day while they were doing that to him. Abu Bakr's house was among the Banu Jumah. He said to Umayya: "Will you not fear Allah the Exalted regarding this poor man?" Umayya said: "You corrupted him, so rescue him from what you see." Abu Bakr said: "I will! I have a black slave, stronger and more robust than him, who holds your religion. Shall I give him to you?" He said: "I accept." So Abu Bakr gave him his slave and took Bilal and freed him. Then he freed, along with him, on Islam, before he emigrated, six [necks] [[In "B": "raqabat" (feminine plural).]], Bilal being the seventh: Amir ibn Fuhayra, who witnessed Badr and Uhud and was killed as a martyr on the day of Bir Ma'una; Umm Umays; and Zinnira. Her sight was struck when he freed her, and the Quraysh said: "Only al-Lat and al-Uzza took away her sight." She said: "They lie, by the House of Allah! Al-Lat and al-Uzza neither harm nor benefit." So Allah restored her sight. He also freed al-Nahdiyya and her daughter, who belonged to a woman of the Banu Abd al-Dar. He passed by them while their mistress had sent them to grind [flour] [[In "B": "tatahanan" (they were grinding).]] for her, and she was saying: "By Allah, I will never free you two!" Abu Bakr said: "Release them, O mother of so-and-so." She said: "You release them, since you corrupted them, so free them." Abu Bakr [may Allah be pleased with him] [[Included in brackets in "B" only.]] said: "For how much?" She said: "For such-and-such." He said: "I have taken them, and they are free." He also passed by a slave girl of the Banu al-Mu'ammal who was being tortured, bought her, and freed her. [[Sirat Ibn Hisham: 1/339-340.]]

Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab said: It reached me that Umayya ibn Khalaf said to Abu Bakr concerning Bilal, when he said: "Will you sell him?" He said: "Yes, I will sell him for Nistas, a slave of Abu Bakr's," who was the owner of ten thousand dinars, along with boys, slave girls and livestock. Nistas was a polytheist. Abu Bakr had urged him toward Islam on condition that his wealth remain his own, but he refused, so Abu Bakr became displeased with him. When Umayya said to him, "I will sell him to you in exchange for your slave Nistas," he seized the opportunity and sold him to him. The polytheists said: "Abu Bakr did not do that for Bilal except because of a favor Bilal had done for him." So Allah revealed:

Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 92, verses 19–21:

﴿And no one has a favour with him that must be repaid,﴾ [[See: al-Tabari 30/228; al-Wahidi, Asbab al-Nuzul, p. 526; al-Durr al-Manthur 8/538.]] meaning: he [Abu Bakr] does not repay him or reciprocate for it.

﴿Except﴾ rather, ﴿seeking the countenance of his Lord, the Most High.﴾ That is: he does not do this as a recompense to anyone for a blessing he received from them; rather, he does it seeking the countenance of his Lord, the Most High, and desiring His good pleasure.

﴿And he will surely be well-pleased.﴾ With what Allah, Mighty and Majestic, will give him in the Hereafter of Paradise and honour, as a reward for what he did.
